Prediction markets aren't part of the spec, but there was an interesting idea floated in [this github issue](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/10).

Thought it could be fun to hold myself accountable.

A few theses:

- Deployment of AI into enterprise will take time

- Within three years, AI deployments translate to meaningful headcount reductions

- The market for cognition experiences a massive supply shock; larger supply of human + AI/computational labor suppresses wages and bargaining power

Stubbing: Stubbing: This is likely an unpopular thought in the thicket, but the return on a lot of labor is going to zero dunno what counts are labor.

Well this is interesting on two levels. 1) The proposed bet. And 2) are prediction markets a part of the Blygger spec and I missed it?

I'm not sure I disagree that we could see a 10% fall in wages, though. But I see what you're saying. If that happened it wouldn't mean everyone's wages were down 10%. It would mean LOADS of people are no longer working. So I see your point. I do think some other kind of work will come along, that's part of what I'm saying. But I don't want to predict too much, because I think it will be weirder than that. Maybe orthogonal to 'work.'

But OK OK I take your point. Let's watch this bet. Kinda scary to think about.
